entities.summary: Arthur O'Connor, was a United Irishman who was active in seeking allies for the Irish cause in England and in France. A proponent of radical democratic reform, in Ireland he was distinguished by publishing political appeals to women. Arrested on the eve of the 1798 rebellion, in 1802 he went into exile in France where, after being raised to the rank of General in a force that was to invade Ireland, fell out of favour with Napoleon. Among the positions he maintained publicly in his final years were a defence of the July Revolution in Paris and opposition to what he saw as the clericalism of Daniel O'Connell's movement in Ireland.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Arthur O'Connor's advocacy for radical democratic reform and his involvement in the Irish cause had a significant impact on Ireland's struggle for independence, particularly through his connections with European powers. His defense of the July Revolution in Paris also highlighted the transnational nature of the struggle.
